Overview
We are a leading global provider of biological and chemical compound sample exploration and management solutions for the life sciences industry. We entered the life sciences market in 2011, leveraging our in-house precision automation and cryogenics capabilities that we were then applying in the semiconductor manufacturing market. This led us to develop and provide solutions for automated ultra-cold storage. Since then, we have expanded our life sciences offerings through internal investments and through a series of acquisitions. We support our customers from research and clinical development to commercialization with our sample management and automated storage systems, as well as genomic services expertise to help our customers bring impactful therapies to market faster. We understand the importance of sample integrity and offer a broad portfolio of products and services supporting customers at every stage of the life cycle of samples, including procurement, automated storage systems, genomic services and a multitude of sample consumables, informatics and data software, along with sample repository services. Our expertise, global footprint, and leadership positions enable us to be a trusted global partner to pharmaceutical, biotechnology and life sciences research institutions. In total, we employ approximately 2,850 full-time employees, part-time employees and contingent workers worldwide as of September 30, 2026 and have sales in approximately 87 countries. We are headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts and have operations in North America, Asia and Europe.
Our Company was founded in 1978 and became a leading automation provider and partner to the global semiconductor manufacturing industry. We divested the last of our semiconductor businesses in February 2022 for $2.9 billion in cash and since then operate solely as a life sciences company. On December 1, 2021, we changed our corporate name from “Brooks Automation, Inc.” to “Azenta, Inc.” and our common stock started to trade on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “AZTA”. We divested our B Medical Systems business in July 2026 for $63.0 million in cash. This strategic action simplified our portfolio and allowed management to focus on driving revenue growth and profitability in our core Sample Management Solutions and Multiomics segments. Both the semiconductor automation results and the B Medical Systems business results are classified as discontinued operations, and, unless otherwise noted, the description of our business in this Annual Report on Form 10-K relates solely to our continuing operations.
Our portfolio includes product and service offerings developed by us internally, as well as obtained through acquisitions, designed to provide comprehensive capabilities to our customers, addressing their needs in sample exploration and management, automated storage and multiomics. We continue to develop new product and service offerings and enhance existing and acquired offerings through the expertise of our research and development resources. We believe our acquisition, investment, and integration approach has allowed us to accelerate internal development and significantly accelerate time to market for our life sciences solutions.
For further information on our acquisitions, please refer to Note 4, Business Combinations to our consolidated financial statements included under Part II, Item 8, “Financial Statements and Supplementary Data” of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
Recent Developments
Leadership Transition
On August 22, 2026, John P. Marotta resigned as our President and Chief Executive Officer and as a director, and our Board of Directors appointed Dr. Martin D. Madaus, a member of the Board since January 2024, as Interim President and Chief Executive Officer. The Board has retained an executive search firm, and a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer is underway.
Multiomics Restructuring Plan
On October 5, 2026, our Board of Directors approved, and we committed to, a restructuring plan within our Multiomics segment intended primarily to consolidate our North American laboratory network, simplify our organizational structure and improve operating efficiency. The plan consists of workforce reductions and the closure of three of our Multiomics laboratory sites in North America. We currently estimate aggregate pre-tax charges of approximately $11.0 million to $13.0 million, consisting primarily of approximately $9.0 million of asset impairment charges and approximately $3.0 million of employee severance and other restructuring charges, substantially all of which we expect to recognize in fiscal year 2027, and we expect to substantially complete the planned actions by March 31, 2027, subject to applicable

Gene Synthesis Investments
On October 28, 2026, we acquired SynPlexity Inc. (“SynPlexity”), a DNA assembly technology company providing products and services centered on large, multiplexed gene libraries, and entered into an exclusive, royalty-free technology license agreement and a master services and supply agreement with Elegen Corp. (“Elegen”) relating to Elegen’s cell-free DNA synthesis technology. We intend to integrate these technologies into our Multiomics segment’s gene synthesis portfolio.
We acquired SynPlexity for a base purchase price of $15.0 million in cash, of which approximately $2.5 million was held back, subject to customary closing and post-closing adjustments. The purchase agreement also provides for contingent consideration of up to $10.0 million based on the achievement of a specified revenue milestone through September 30, 2029. Due to the timing of the acquisition, the initial accounting for the business combination is incomplete, and certain disclosures related to the acquisition are not yet available.
Under the license agreement with Elegen, the license has an initial five-year term and requires fixed license payments totaling $23.0 million, subject to certain retained rights and exceptions in favor of Elegen. We have an option, exercisable between 12 and 18 months after execution, to convert the license into an irrevocable, perpetual, exclusive, royalty-free license for $25.0 million, plus any then-unpaid license fees, subject to the license’s term. We currently expect aggregate capital deployment under the Elegen arrangements to range from approximately $32.0 million to approximately $71.0 million, depending on the extent of our future capital equipment purchases and whether we exercise the conversion option.
Life Sciences Market
Our businesses serve a broad range of end markets within the life sciences industry to help our customers advance the development of therapies to improve people’s lives and cure diseases. With the advent of biologics and personalized medicine, biological samples have become critical assets to the success of drug and therapy pipelines, and the proper management and protection of these samples are important to our customers. As a result, we believe there is a sizable market opportunity for us to provide comprehensive sample management and genomic solutions.
Since the successful mapping of the full human genome at the turn of this century, the market for genomic services has grown in support of research in biologic drug development, personalized medicine, and cell and gene therapy, or CGT. Pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies and institutions may use their in-house laboratory resources to sequence millions of genes as part of their research workflows. Many companies and institutions outsource all or a part of their gene sequencing to independent laboratories that provide expedited results and expert consultation services. We participate in this market as a value-added laboratory services provider, offering high quality genetic testing services with fast turnaround times and expert customer support.
We have approximately 11,000 customers globally and believe we are well positioned to expand our customer base. We serve top pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, the most advanced research hospitals performing clinical research and therapy development, as well as some of the newest and leading-edge start-ups in the biotech space. In addition, we serve academic and government institutions. Demand varies by offering and region; for example, in fiscal year 2026, revenue from Sample Repository Services and Consumables and Instruments increased, while revenue from Automated Stores and Sanger sequencing services declined. The forward-looking statements in this report are qualified by these risk factors.
Risk Factor Summary
The following summarizes the principal risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations or the value of our common stock. This summary should be read together with the full risk factors that follow.
Business, Market and Strategic Risks
• Demand for our products and services may decline or fluctuate because of economic conditions, reductions or delays in government and academic research funding, customer capital-spending constraints, interest rates, inflation, changing product and service mix, competitive pricing and other factors.
• Rapid technological change, including AI-enabled discovery, laboratory automation and integrated design, synthesis, sequencing and analysis workflows, may change customer requirements and the volume or mix of services they purchase. If we do not innovate, commercialize new offerings and deploy AI effectively, our offerings may become less competitive or obsolete and our investments may not produce expected benefits.
• Our transformation, restructuring, acquisition, investment and integration activities may be delayed, cost more than expected, disrupt operations, fail to achieve anticipated benefits, or result in additional impairment charges.
• Our operating results may vary significantly, and inaccurate demand forecasts may cause excess or obsolete inventory, underutilized capacity, expedited costs or an inability to meet customer demand.
Global, Regulatory and Supply-Chain Risks
• Our global operations expose us to political, economic, legal, tax, currency, anti-corruption and regulatory risks, particularly in China and other jurisdictions where requirements may conflict or change rapidly.
• Geopolitical tensions, tariffs, export controls, sanctions, the BIOSECURE Act and restrictions on transfers of genomic samples or sensitive data may increase costs, constrain our China-based operations or suppliers, reduce demand, require changes in workflows or capacity, and weaken our competitiveness.
• We depend on sole- or limited-source suppliers, specialized components, instruments, consumables and raw materials. Supplier failures, shortages, quality problems, trade restrictions or logistics disruptions could interrupt manufacturing or services, and qualifying alternatives may be costly, time-consuming or unsuccessful.
• Expanded regulation of our products, genomic services, laboratories, gene synthesis, biosecurity, conflict minerals, environmental practices and health and safety could require operational changes and additional investment or result in fines, suspensions, customer losses or reputational harm.
Operational, Technology and Data Risks
• Disruptions at our laboratories, manufacturing sites, sample repositories or information systems, including from severe weather, utility failures, equipment failures, public-health events, cyberattacks or other unexpected events, could damage customer samples, interrupt operations and harm our reputation.
• Cybersecurity incidents affecting us or our service providers could disrupt operations; compromise customer, genomic, personal, confidential or proprietary information; result in theft or loss; and expose us to remediation costs, litigation, regulatory action and reputational harm.
• Our collection, processing and cross-border transfer of personal, health, genomic and other sensitive data are subject to evolving and sometimes conflicting privacy and data-protection laws. Noncompliance could restrict our activities and result in significant penalties, claims and costs.

Financial Reporting, Asset and Tax Risks
• A remaining material weakness in internal control over financial reporting may result in material misstatements, delayed or inaccurate reporting, remediation costs, regulatory consequences and reduced investor confidence.
• Our goodwill, intangible assets and other long-lived assets may be impaired if performance, forecasts, market conditions, stock price or valuation assumptions deteriorate, resulting in material non-cash charges.
• Changes in tax laws, audits, valuation allowances, limitations on net operating losses, challenges to tax positions or restrictions on repatriating foreign cash could increase our tax expense and reduce liquidity.
Intellectual Property, Customers and Third Parties
• We may be unable to obtain, maintain or enforce IP protection; our patents may expire or be challenged; or we may face infringement claims that require costly litigation, licensing, or restrictions on our offerings.
• Customers often purchase through individual orders without long-term commitments and may reduce, delay or discontinue purchases.
• Product, service or storage failures that damage customer materials or produce inaccurate results could create substantial liability and reputational harm.
• Third-party providers may fail to perform, suffer cybersecurity incidents or mishandle sensitive information, disrupting our operations and exposing us to liability, despite our diligence and contractual protections.
Risks Relating to Our Common Stock
• Our stock price may remain volatile due to operating performance, market conditions, activism and other factors. Stockholder activism or securities litigation may impose significant costs, divert management and Board attention, constrain capital-allocation decisions and affect our ability to retain personnel.
• Our charter documents, preferred-stock authorization and Delaware law may delay or prevent a change in control or otherwise adversely affect the rights or market value of our common stock.
